templates.name: TacticalRMM (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for ansible/playbooks/tacticalrmm/tacticalrmm_server.yml -- covers TacticalRMM AND its bundled MeshCentral in ONE template (Robert's explicit 2026-10-20 call: the standalone meshcentral playbook is retired, EXAMSHCLD001 decommissioned, TacticalRMM's own bundled instance is the real, live replacement; no separate meshcentral template was built). Copied from zabbix_template_bind9.json's own generator and extended with httptests (web scenarios) -- the FIRST template in this series to use that object type, following a shopping-list-first review of the full 2808-line playbook.

*** DOES NOT STANDALONE-IMPORT *** -- same reasoning as bind9 (template 6): this template does NOT declare nodeinfo.json's master item or its 15-field base schema (every one of templates 1-5 still does, independently, a known deferred-fix backlog item -- see feedback_zabbix_duplicate_item_keys_across_templates.md). This template's one nodeinfo_extra item (section O) is a DEPENDENT item referencing linuxtools' own master key by name. Link the linuxtools template to any host before (or together with) this one.

SECTIONS
  A. Packages (12): rmm_base_packages minus common_packages overlap, plus the install-time functional packages (nginx/nodejs/postgresql-18/redis).
  B. Systemd service state (11): is-active via system.run (classic agent only -- NOT the agent2-only systemd.unit.info key), anchored regexp trigger (avoids the 'active' being a substring of 'inactive' trap a plain 'like' match would hit).
  C. Listening ports (7): 443/80/9235 confirmed directly from this playbook's own nginx configs; 5432/6379/4430 are each service's own well-known/configured default. NATS's own client port is UNCONFIRMED (nats-rmm.conf is generated dynamically, not templated anywhere) -- {$TACTICALRMM.NATS_PORT} macro defaults to NATS's documented default (4222), flagged for live confirmation. No UDP component anywhere in this stack.
  D. Web scenarios (3, httptests): frontend/backend/MeshCentral vhosts, verify_peer/verify_host left at their documented default (0/skip -- the shared cert is self-signed by design, TRMM_INSECURE=True, so skip-verification is exactly the behaviour wanted; the two fields' own export-format string encoding wasn't confirmed against a real example, unlike follow_redirects, so they're omitted rather than guessed) -- doubles as a DNS-resolution check (category 14's own ask: bind9's template can't know whether an RMM subdomain SHOULD resolve, this one can). status_codes not pinned to one exact value -- NOT YET LIVE-TESTED, tune once real responses are seen. Triggers on the auto-created web.test.fail[<scenario>] item, not a manually-declared one.
  E. Config/script files (12): 9 files (nginx.conf/celery.conf/7 systemd units) get exists+cksum -- their content is either fully static or templated only with a fixed group_vars constant (rmm_service_user), so a single expected cksum is genuinely stable; cksums computed by parsing the real YAML with PyYAML, never retyped by hand. The 3 nginx SITE configs are exists-only -- their content embeds live, per-host facts (rmm_domain/subdomains), no single stable expected value.
  F. Secret-bearing files (4): exists-only (contents never read) + a mode-drift check (system.run + stat -- no native classic-agent key reads file permissions). Triggers on ANY drift from the expected mode, not just more-permissive.
  G. Install markers (3): INFORMATION severity only -- install-phase completion, not an active-outage signal.
  H. TLS certificate expiry: classic-agent has no built-in cert-expiry key (web.certificate.get is Zabbix AGENT 2 ONLY, confirmed against the real docs, not usable under this estate's classic-agent-only policy) -- system.run + openssl + date instead, same UserParameter-equivalent idiom already used everywhere else in this series. WARNING/HIGH two-stage trigger on the same item ({$TACTICALRMM.CERT_WARN_DAYS}/{$TACTICALRMM.CERT_HIGH_DAYS}).
  I. UFW: count-based ALLOW-rule check (package + service-active already covered in A/B) -- not matched against exact status-output column formatting, not independently confirmed live.
  J. PostgreSQL: DELIBERATELY no live psql existence check for the 2 DBs/roles -- the zabbix-agent OS user has no confirmed permission path to query PostgreSQL, and granting one would be a new security-relevant sudoers/pg_hba change, Robert's call to make, not assumed here. Service-active + port-listening (A/B/C) are the practical proxies.
  K. Git repo drift (4): /rmm and /opt/trmm-community-scripts, both world-readable clones -- branch + dirty-count, same shape as the ansible-node template's own repo checks.
  L. Python venv integrity: backend venv's own python binary exists.
  M. Celery liveness (4): proc.num[] (a real classic-agent built-in key -- deliberately NOT a kill -0 pidfile check, which would silently misreport EPERM-under-a-different-UID as 'process doesn't exist', a real false-positive trap avoided here) beyond systemd's own 'active' state, which only proves the wrapper launched. Process-name patterns not independently confirmed live.
  N. Log growth (2, with WARNING/HIGH two-stage triggers): no logrotate existed for celery or the backend vhost's nginx private logs before this round -- FIXED DIRECTLY in tacticalrmm_server.yml itself (Robert's explicit go-ahead, 2026-10-20). These items are the ongoing guard on top of that fix, {$TACTICALRMM.LOG_WARN_BYTES} for WARNING, double that for HIGH.
  O. nodeinfo.json extras: static_ip only. rmm_install_status is deliberately excluded from monitoring (a human-readable sentence, not a stable monitorable value) -- but its underlying staleness bug (permanently describing Phase 1 only, on every box regardless of real completion) WAS fixed directly in tacticalrmm_server.yml's own Section 20, same round.

NOT YET LIVE-IMPORTED OR LIVE-TESTED against a real Zabbix server or a real zabbix-agent -- same status as every other template in this series. The httptests block (section D) is this series' first use of that object type --  double-check it specifically on first import.

REAL LIVE FINDING, 2026-10-24: first TWO import attempts rejected with "Invalid tag .../template(1): unexpected tag 'triggers'" -- the 3 template-level triggers here (web.test.fail checks, which can't nest under a regular item the way every other trigger in this series does, since web.test.fail items are auto-generated by the httptest itself, not declared in items[]) were nested INSIDE the template object (first right after items[], then after httptests[] on the second attempt -- reordering within the template object never fixed it, because that was never the real problem). ROOT CAUSE, confirmed via Robert's own live configuration.export of a real throwaway httptest+trigger built directly in the Zabbix 7.0 UI: "triggers" for an httptest-derived item is NOT a field on the template object AT ALL -- it's a SIBLING of "templates" at the zabbix_export ROOT level, collecting triggers across the whole export, same shape as template_groups/templates. Moved the 3 triggers out of the template object entirely, up to zabbix_export.triggers (docs/zabbix_templates/import_template.py's own import_rules() already has a top-level "triggers" rule entry for exactly this). CONFIRMED structurally correct against Robert's live ground truth. Two more rejections followed, both now fixed in the SAME pass along with a full field-by-field audit of this whole section (not just the one reported error each time): the httptest step object also had an invalid "uuid" (removed) and an invalid "no" (removed -- step order is implicit from array position, same as every other array in this series); each httptest object itself also had a "status": "ENABLED" field never present in the ground truth (removed -- matches the default anyway, so no functional change, just matching the proven-valid shape literally instead of carrying an extra untested field). Also audited macros/tags (structurally identical to linuxtools' own, already proven), the items[] block (never flagged by any import attempt so far, implying it was already clean), and the parent-template "templates" link (same pattern as bind9's own confirmed-working fix). Every httptest/step field remaining now matches EXACTLY what Robert's own live configuration.export produced for a real, working scenario+trigger -- not re-attempted against the real server yet.

ALSO FIXED same pass, same root cause as bind9's own 2026-10-24 finding (see that template's own description): this template's nodeinfo: static_ip item references linuxtools' master key but had no parent-template declaration of its own. Added the same top-level "templates" entry naming linuxtools_examplemusic -- this hadn't surfaced yet in the live error above since the triggers-ordering rejection happens first, but would have failed the exact same way bind9 did on the very next attempt. UNVERIFIED, same as the triggers reorder above.

IMPORT: configuration.import, rules: createMissing+updateExisting+deleteMissing on items/triggers/httptests, createMissing+updateExisting on template_groups/templates.

items.name: Service active: rmm
items.description: systemctl is-active rmm, via system.run (classic zabbix-agent, AllowKey=system.run[*] already deployed by tasks/zabbix_agent_onboard.yml). Trigger uses an anchored regexp (^active$), not a substring 'like' match -- 'active' is a literal substring of 'inactive', a plain like-match would wrongly pass a stopped service.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - rmm is not active
triggers.description: rmm is not reporting active (stopped/failed/activating). Check: systemctl status rmm && journalctl -u rmm -n 100.

items.name: TLS certificate expiry (epoch seconds)
items.description: UNIX epoch of /etc/ssl/tactical/cert.pem's own notAfter date (the one self-signed cert shared by all 3 vhosts, 3650-day validity from Section 15). No native classic-agent key for this -- web.certificate.get is Zabbix Agent 2 only, not usable under this estate's classic-agent-only policy.

triggers.expression: last(/TacticalRMM (Example Music)/system.run[openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/ssl/tactical/cert.pem | cut -d= -f2 | xargs -I{} date -d {} +%s,wait])-now()<{$TACTICALRMM.CERT_WARN_DAYS}*86400
triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - TLS certificate expires within {$TACTICALRMM.CERT_WARN_DAYS} days
triggers.description: The shared self-signed cert is approaching expiry. Re-run tacticalrmm_server.yml's Section 15 cert-generation task (or regenerate manually) well before it lapses -- an expired cert breaks all 3 vhosts' TLS handshakes at once.

triggers.expression: last(/TacticalRMM (Example Music)/system.run[openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/ssl/tactical/cert.pem | cut -d= -f2 | xargs -I{} date -d {} +%s,wait])-now()<{$TACTICALRMM.CERT_HIGH_DAYS}*86400
triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - TLS certificate expires within {$TACTICALRMM.CERT_HIGH_DAYS} days (critical)
triggers.description: The shared self-signed cert is in its final critical window before expiry -- regenerate it now.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - web check failed: TacticalRMM frontend
triggers.description: The 'TacticalRMM frontend' web scenario failed its step. Covers nginx + the backing service + TLS handshake + DNS resolution for this vhost all at once -- check web.test.error[TacticalRMM frontend] for the actual error text. Static SPA served directly by nginx (try_files ... /index.html) -- the most deterministic of the 3, hence the tight status_codes.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - web check failed: TacticalRMM API backend
triggers.description: The 'TacticalRMM API backend' web scenario failed its step. Covers nginx + the backing service + TLS handshake + DNS resolution for this vhost all at once -- check web.test.error[TacticalRMM API backend] for the actual error text. Django REST API root -- exact expected response not live-verified, range excludes 5xx (upstream uwsgi dead) and connection failure.

triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - web check failed: MeshCentral
triggers.description: The 'MeshCentral' web scenario failed its step. Covers nginx + the backing service + TLS handshake + DNS resolution for this vhost all at once -- check web.test.error[MeshCentral] for the actual error text. Reverse-proxied to 127.0.0.1:4430 -- exact expected response not live-verified, tolerates a redirect.
